sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page romk1240 (Hammarström et al.), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: No descriptive references; only Z'graggen 1969: 151-155 (subclassification) and Campbell et al. 2022 (AES 'shifting'). Links to OLAC, IMTVault, ELP.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. A. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. Handle 1885/252975.
sources.note: Romkun appears only in the Tamolan family listing / map key; zero hits for stress, accent, tone.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. Handle 1885/146484.
sources.note: Romkun (M9, pop. 389; villages Romkun 1, Romkun 2) only in language, village and census lists; zero hits for stress, accent, tone.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Iski language' (Romkun redirect) and 'Tamolan languages' (Usher 2020 Proto-Tamolan phoneme reconstruction), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Breri and Romkun treated as dialects of one 'Iski' language; proto-consonant/vowel inventory only.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: Romkun; Breri-Romkun; Iski pages (Internet Archive copy 2019-03-21 and 2020-10-16).
sources.note: Page bodies read '[under construction]' for Situation, Sources and Pronouns; no data.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19, handle 1885/146580.
sources.note: Nothing on stress (zero hits for stress/accent in the whole book). Only phonological remark on Romkun, p. 82, sect. 2.23.22.3 'Typological Characteristics of Tamolan' item 6: 'Romkun is possibly tonal, and voiced and voiceless nasals seem to occur.' Sect. 2.23.22.15 (p. 82): 'Romkun 63/Ro (350). Spoken in Romkun and other small hamlets. Previously unrecorded.'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. DOI 10.25911/5d739250d08c9, handle 1885/130077.
sources.note: p. 13 (general, all wordlists): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' p. 155: same 'Romkun is possibly tonal, and voiced and voiceless nasals seem to occur.' No Romkun stress statement.

sources.note: SIL PNG alphabet-development worksheets normally contain a short phonology summary (phoneme chart, syllable, stress/tone remarks) as the basis for orthography decisions; this is the only description-type document for Romkun proper and the most likely place for a stress statement.
